title: 「Just because X does not mean Y」句
titleZh: 「Just because X does not mean Y」反駁沒有充分根據的結論
titleEn: Just because X does not mean Y

source.file: Sentence Structure 252 -「Just because X does not mean Y——反駁沒有充分根據的結論」.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.
The source filename is numbered one lower than this system lesson ID because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formula: Just because + X clause + does not mean + Y clause / noun phrase

formulas.formula: Just because + X clause + does not mean + Y clause / noun phrase
It does not mean + Y + just because + X
Subject + remember / understand / recognise + that + just because X does not mean Y
Subject + explained / argued / warned / pointed out + that + just because X did not mean Y
One point / fact / lesson is clear: just because X does not mean Y

example: Just because the book is long does not mean it is difficult.
exampleZh: 這本書很長，並不代表它很難。

examples.en: Just because the book is long does not mean it is difficult.
examples.zh: 這本書很長，並不代表它很難。
examples.highlight: Just because the book is long does not mean it is difficult.

examples.en: It does not mean you have failed just because you made one mistake.
examples.zh: 你犯了一次錯，並不代表你已經失敗。
examples.highlight: It does not mean you have failed just because you made one mistake.

examples.en: We must recognise that just because someone disagrees does not mean they are wrong.
examples.zh: 我們必須明白，有人不同意並不代表他們是錯的。
examples.highlight: We must recognise that just because someone disagrees does not mean they are wrong.

meaning.zh: 用來說明某個事實、理由或情況並不足以證明另一個結論，從而反駁過早或欠缺根據的推論。

rules.zh: X 是已知的事實、理由或情況；Y 是不應自動推出的結論。
rules.en: X is a fact, reason or situation; Y is a conclusion that does not necessarily follow.

rules.zh: 這個句型不一定表示 Y 是錯的，只表示 X 單獨不足以證明 Y。
rules.en: The structure does not always claim that Y is definitely false. It says that X alone is not enough to prove Y.

rules.zh: 標準現在式使用 does not mean，不使用 do not mean。
rules.en: Use does not mean in the standard present-tense form because the complete just because clause is treated as one idea.

rules.zh: 如結論屬過去情況或過去報告，可使用 did not mean。
rules.en: Use did not mean when the conclusion belongs to a past situation or a past report.

rules.zh: Y 可接完整子句、情態動詞子句、否定子句或名詞短語。
rules.en: Y may be a complete clause, a modal clause, a negative clause or a noun phrase.

rules.zh: 標準句首形式中，just because 子句作 does not mean 的主語，通常不加逗號。
rules.en: In the standard initial pattern, the just because clause functions as the subject of does not mean, so a comma is normally unnecessary.

benefits.zh: 有助反駁沒有充分根據或過早作出的假設。
benefits.en: It helps you challenge a weak assumption.

benefits.zh: 能清楚分開已知事實和未被證明的推論，使推理更嚴謹。
benefits.en: It makes your reasoning more careful.

benefits.zh: 能在一句內把假設和修正連接起來。
benefits.en: It combines an assumption and its correction.

benefits.zh: 適合在討論、議論文、簡報和日常對話中回應過度簡化的看法。
benefits.en: It is useful in discussions and argumentative writing.

benefits.zh: 可以堅定地反駁結論，同時不必直接說對方錯誤。
benefits.en: It helps you sound firm without being rude.

benefits.zh: 目標關係可出現在句首、句中、認知動詞後、報告動詞後或冒號後。
benefits.en: It gives you genuine sentence variety.

questions.answerZh: 我們不應忘記，一項服務免費並不代表提供它不需要成本。
questions.highlight: We must not forget that just because a service is free does not mean it has no cost to provide.

questions.prompt: Technology can make a task faster without improving the final decision.
questions.promptZh: 科技可以加快完成任務，但不一定能改善最終決定。
questions.answer: Just because technology makes a task faster does not mean it makes the final decision better.
questions.answerZh: 科技令任務更快完成，並不代表它能改善最終決定。
questions.highlight: Just because technology makes a task faster does not mean it makes the final decision better.

questions.prompt: The organisation had followed the rules, but the review panel concluded that it might still have acted unfairly.
questions.promptZh: 該機構遵守了規則，但審查小組認為它的做法仍可能不公平。
questions.answer: The review panel concluded that just because the organisation had followed the rules did not mean it had acted fairly.
questions.answerZh: 審查小組認為，該機構遵守了規則並不代表它的做法公平。
questions.highlight: The review panel concluded that just because the organisation had followed the rules did not mean it had acted fairly.

questions.prompt: A tradition can exist for generations without needing to remain unchanged.
questions.promptZh: 一項傳統即使已存在多代，也不一定需要維持不變。
questions.answer: It does not mean a tradition should remain unchanged just because it has existed for generations.
questions.answerZh: 一項傳統已存在多代，並不代表它應該維持不變。
questions.highlight: It does not mean a tradition should remain unchanged just because it has existed for generations.

questions.prompt: Examination results had improved, but the head teacher said some students might still lack the support they needed.
questions.promptZh: 考試成績有所改善，但校長表示部分學生可能仍未獲得所需的支援。
questions.answer: The head teacher emphasised that just because examination results had improved did not mean every student was receiving the support they needed.
questions.answerZh: 校長強調，考試成績有所改善並不代表每名學生都正獲得所需的支援。
questions.highlight: The head teacher emphasised that just because examination results had improved did not mean every student was receiving the support they needed.

questions.prompt: A solution may work in the short term without remaining effective in the long term.
questions.promptZh: 一個解決方法即使短期內有效，也不一定能長期維持成效。
questions.answer: Just because a solution works in the short term does not mean it will remain effective in the long term.
questions.answerZh: 一個解決方法短期內有效，並不代表它能長期維持成效。
questions.highlight: Just because a solution works in the short term does not mean it will remain effective in the long term.

questions.prompt: An idea may challenge common beliefs and still be correct. We should recognise this.
questions.promptZh: 一個想法即使挑戰普遍觀念，仍然可能是正確的。我們應該明白這一點。
questions.answer: We should recognise that just because an idea challenges common beliefs does not mean it is wrong.
questions.answerZh: 我們應該明白，一個想法挑戰普遍觀念並不代表它是錯的。
questions.highlight: We should recognise that just because an idea challenges common beliefs does not mean it is wrong.
